name: grotto-skills
description: Public Grotto developer skills for HTML5/WebGL game creators.

skills.name: grotto-game-runtime-developer-sdk
skills.summary: Core Grotto Runtime SDK guide for trusted identity, bounded cloud sessions, saves, events, capability-gated inventory, and one-use public multiplayer bootstrap tickets.

skills.name: grotto-core-of-gaming
skills.summary: Core game-design principles for shaping clear challenge, meaningful choices, readable feedback, fair progression, game feel, and a complete entertaining loop.
skills.inject: Core of Gaming — build around a clear player fantasy and one primary challenge (execution, perception, reasoning, strategy, risk, social understanding, expression, or discovery). Define 2–4 verbs and a repeatable loop: goal → obstacle → player action/decision → legible consequence → learning → another meaningfully different attempt. Make tradeoffs real; use randomness to create situations, not replace decisions. Teach one idea safely, test it, then combine it. Make failure attributable and fair, with one-action recovery. Use sound, animation, particles, camera, and HUD response to clarify mechanics and reward mastery; polish amplifies the loop, it does not replace it. Put the first meaningful action within about 15–20 seconds, show goal/controls without a tutorial wall, test both success and failure, and prefer one small complete loop over broad unfinished features. Before finishing, playtest dominant strategies, softlocks, idle/rapid input, resize, touch, restart, and whether the Game invites one more try.

skills.name: grotto-game-token-gated-inventory
skills.summary: Token-gate Grotto game content using capability-gated exact ERC-1155/ERC-721 balances over the immutable verified-wallet launch snapshot.
skills.inject: Token-gated content — use `grotto.getInventory()` only when the exact game ID has `inventory:read` enabled by platform policy. The platform checks the immutable private canonical-plus-linked wallet snapshot, applies any per-game contract filter, proves complete pagination, and returns exact decimal-string balances to parse with `BigInt`. Treat missing scope, `503`, invalid data, or `partial !== false` as no gated entitlement; keep only free/default content available. Account-link changes require a new play session. Do not add wallet selectors or trust `checkedAt` as chain-read time; default source staleness is bounded to 45 seconds.

skills.name: grotto-hosted-game-github-workflow
skills.summary: Maintain Grotto games with GitHub, CI, hosted clients, a secure runtime wrapper, and replay-safe authoritative inventory/multiplayer services.
skills.inject: Hosted-game workflow — deploy the real client to Railway/Vercel and upload a tiny root wrapper that forwards `grotto:runtime` only from its parent to the known hosted origin. Coordinate exact per-game inventory/multiplayer allowlists after publication. For realtime, request a fresh ticket on every connect/reconnect, verify the strict Ed25519/version/time/game/public-room profile, atomically consume UUIDv4 `jti` in shared storage, then authorize party/queue/ranked placement server-side. Cache JWKS by `kid`, refresh unknown keys, and support current-plus-overlap public-key rotation. Use only with a durable hosted domain.

skills.name: grotto-studio-game-updates
skills.summary: How a creator updates a game in Grotto Studio so the new version reaches players instantly — iterating with B.O.B., keeping cloud saves intact, and rolling back.
skills.inject: Updating a live game — in Grotto Studio every change is a new build that becomes the version players load on their next session: no re-upload, no redeploy, instant for the creator. Keep the root `index.html` entry stable, prefer small targeted edits (so updates are fast and rollback-able), and never break a working save format without migrating it.

skills.name: grotto-pixel-art-assets
skills.summary: Make game assets cheaply: draw pixel art procedurally in code (free), convert any image to crisp pixel art at runtime (free, zero-dep pixelify), and use cheap AI image generation for sprites/textures when you need raster art.
skills.inject: Game assets — make them CHEAP. (1) DEFAULT to drawing pixel art in code: define sprites/tiles as a palette + index grid and paint them to an offscreen canvas (imageSmoothingEnabled=false). Free, deterministic, recolorable, tiny. (2) Convert any raster image to crisp pixel art at runtime with a zero-dep canvas pixelify (hard downscale -> optional palette snap -> nearest-neighbor upscale). (3) For rich raster art, the generate_image tool is cheap and on every tier — pass pixel:true for pixel-art sprites; transparent:true for sprites/items. Keep pixels crisp everywhere: CSS image-rendering:pixelated, ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled=false, Three.js NearestFilter. Bias toward code; use AI images to accent, not carry.
